I can do that — but I can’t watch for finance sign-off in the background. I need an explicit go‑ahead (and access to the workbook) to perform destructive edits. Before I proceed I need to confirm a few details.

Planned steps I’ll take when you confirm:
1. Make a backup copy of the workbook (recommended). I’ll name it "<original name> — backup before assumptions delete" unless you prefer a different name.
2. In the Plan sheet, replace formulas in column H with their current values (I will paste values only). I will operate on the used range of column H (not the entire infinite column) unless you tell me otherwise.
3. Delete the Assumptions tab (permanently remove that sheet).
4. Save and report back with what I changed (which rows were converted, backup name, and confirmation that Assumptions was deleted).

Please confirm these items and provide any preferences:
- Spreadsheet to edit / grant access (or upload it here).
- Exact sheet name to delete (you wrote "old assumptions tab" — is the sheet named "Assumptions" exactly?).
- Column H scope: use the entire column, or only from row X to row Y, or “used range” (recommended).
- Do you want a backup copy made? If yes, any preferred backup name (or I’ll use the default above).
- Do you want me to add a note in the workbook (e.g., a comment in Plan!H1 or a changelog sheet) stating who/when the change was made?

If you want me to run this now, reply with a confirmation like:
"CONFIRM: proceed now — backup yes, backup name: [name], delete sheet: Assumptions, Plan column H: used range."
Once you confirm and provide access, I’ll inspect the workbook and proceed.
